nodes.name: Galvanic Replacement with Kirkendall Effect
nodes.procedure: The Pt/Ni(OH)_2 catalyst was synthesized under weakly acidic conditions using a wet chemical galvanic replacement strategy. Specifically, under acidic conditions, the spontaneous redox reaction occurs between Pt^{4+} and Ni. The Kirkendall effect caused by the different diffusion rates of Ni and Pt atoms led to the formation of platinum-rich nanocages, which were embedded in 3D poriferous Ni(OH)_2.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM records morphology evolution of Pt/Ni(OH)₂ during synthesis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the catalyst during the whole reaction was recorded by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) (Figures S1, S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pore size distribution shows Pt nanocages ~10 nm and Ni(OH)₂ 10-80 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pore size distribution results from N₂ isothermal adsorption measurements show that the pore size of the Pt nanocages is ∼10 nm with 10 - 80 nm for Ni(OH)₂ (Figures S4, S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: 3D TEM tomography confirms Pt nanocages (30-50 nm diameter) uniformly embedded in poriferous Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images of Pt/Ni(OH)₂ observed from different directions (30°,60°,90°, -30°, -60° and -90° as shown in Figure 1b) confirm that Pt nanocages are uniformly embedded in poriferous Ni(OH)₂, exhibiting a diameter of 30 - 50 nm (Figure S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes show Pt (200) at 1.98 Å, (111) at 2.29 Å (angle 54.74°), Ni(OH)₂ (100) at 2.70 Å; random ordered/disordered Ni(OH)₂ fringes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1c, lattice fringes with distinct interplanar distances of 1.98 and 2.29Å can be observed, which are close to the (200) and (111) planes of face-centered cubic phase Pt, respectively. The acute angle between the two planes is 54.74°. ... The lattice fringes with distinct interplanar distances of 2.70Å are assigned to the (100) plane of Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM mapping shows uniform Ni and O distribution, Pt aggregated on nanocages.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) mapping exhibits the uniform distribution of Ni and O species, whereas the Pt species are aggregated on nanocages (Figures 1d and S10).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/Ni(OH)₂ composition: Ni 46.14 wt%, Pt 12.68 wt%; post-HER Pt leaching: Pt/Ni(OH)₂ ~1.12%, Pt/C 7.81%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni and Pt contents of Pt/N_i(OH)_2 determined by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) were 46.14 and 12.68 wt% respectively (Table S1). ... We further quantified the detachment of Pt from Pt/C and Pt/Ni(OH)₂ at 10 mA/cm² by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). As shown in Figure 2g, the total Pt detachment from Pt/Ni(OH)₂ is ∼1.12% which is much lower than that of Pt/C (7.81%).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD consistent with Ni(OH)₂ (100) plane at 2.70 Å (Figure S9).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice fringes with distinct interplanar distances of 2.70Å are assigned to the (100) plane of Ni(OH)₂, consistent with crystallographic information from X-ray diffraction (XRD) (Figure S9).

nodes.characterization_summary: IL-TEM shows Pt/C degradation (carbon migration, Pt detachment, Ostwald ripening 2.80→3.24 nm); Pt/Ni(OH)₂ maintains structure post-HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ identical-location TEM (IL-TEM) was utilized to spatially track structural evolution... The analysis of commercial Pt/C after HER reveals significant carbon support migration and Pt nanoparticles detaching from the substrate (Figure 2b). Concurrently, the Ostwald ripening occurred, increasing the mean Pt particle diameter from 2.80 to 3.24 nm (Figure S11). In contrast, after HER highly dispersed Pt nanocages within poriferous Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets were still observed...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/C Pt content 19.24→13.91 wt% post-HER; Pt/Ni(OH)₂ Pt content stable; K⁺ accumulates at Pt/C Pt-carbon interfaces but uniform on Pt/Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further demonstrate the stability of the active sites in the catalysts, we analyzed the Pt content of Pt/C and Pt/Ni(OH)₂ before and after HER by using EDS. The Pt/C underwent significant metal loss with Pt content decreasing from 19.24 to 13.91 wt%, whereas the Pt content of Pt/Ni(OH)₂ remained almost unchanged... The EDS elemental maps reveal the difference in the location distributions of K⁺ on the Pt/C and Pt/Ni(OH)₂ after HER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p binding energy shift indicates increased Ni valence; Pt 4f negative shift vs H-Pt indicates decreased Pt valence; unchanged post-HER; K detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In XPS, the Ni 2p binding energy of Pt/Ni(OH)₂ is larger than that of H-Ni(OH)₂, and the 4f peak of Pt in Pt/Ni(OH)₂ shows a negative shift compared to H-Pt.[37] This indicates a decrease in the Pt valence state and an increase in the Ni valence state, which is consistent with the XPS results (Figure S18). ... XPS also confirms that the surface chemical state of Pt/Ni(OH)₂ is not altered after HER (Figure S25).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/Ni(OH)₂ white line between Pt foil and PtO (downshift vs H-Pt), indicating moderately positive Pt charge enriched with electrons.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt L₃-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra demonstrated that the white line intensity of Pt/Ni(OH)₂ and H-Pt... was situated between those of Pt foil and PtO, which indicates Pt carried a moderately positive charge.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/Ni(OH)₂ Pt-Pt peaks at 1.99 Å, 2.51 Å; Pt-O peaks shifted to 0.92 Å, 1.38 Å vs PtO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra revealed that Pt/N_i(OH)_2 presented two prominent peaks at 1.99Å and 2.51Å are attributable to the Pt-Pt bond. Compared with PtO (0.76Å and 1.28Å), the Pt-O peaks of Pt/N_i(OH)_2 shift to a lower radial distance with 0.92Å and 1.38Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/Ni(OH)₂ absorption edge more positive than NiO, more negative than H-Ni(OH)₂, indicating Ni valence > +2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: While in the Ni K-edge XANES spectra (Figure 3d), the absorption edges of Pt/Ni(OH)₂ are more positive compared to NiO and more negative compared to H-Ni(OH)₂... which indicates that the Ni atoms in Pt/Ni(OH)₂ display higher valence states than +2.

properties.description: Normalized X-ray absorption near edge structure at Ni K-edge

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/Ni(OH)₂ Ni-O 1.53 Å, Ni-Ni 2.60 Å (vs H-Ni(OH)₂ 1.65 Å, 2.73 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Simultaneously, the Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra show that the Ni-O and Ni-Ni peaks changed from 1.65Å and 2.73Å in H-Ni(OH)₂ to 1.53Å and 2.60Å in Pt/N_i(OH)_2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/C -19.30 mV, Pt/Ni(OH)₂ -9.70 mV in 1 M KOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S20 the zeta potential of Pt/C (−19.30 mV) is more negative than that of Pt/Ni(OH)₂ (−9.70 mV) in 1 M KOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: H_upd peak area decreases 36.8% for Pt/C, 3.5% for Pt/Ni(OH)₂ post-HER, indicating Pt/Ni(OH)₂ active site stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The measured hydrogen underpotential deposition (H_upd) peak area results showed that the H_upd area of Pt/C decreased by 36.8% and that of Pt/Ni(OH)₂ decreased by 3.5%.
